title: NKP
content:
Overview

Overview of the development process used in NKP project.

82044525701819953765nkp_devops_overview.drawio111https://i-p-e-x.atlassian.net/wikinkp_devops_overview.drawio791471


  • A team member picks the story and starts working on it.
  • The Feature branch is named with the JIRA ticket number.
  • Once the developer perceives the task to be done a pull request is created.
  • The pull request is ran through the automated test pipeline where it has to pass all unit, functional and integration tests.
  • The pull request gets reviewed by at least 2 team members.
  • When the pull request is approved it can be merged.
  • Once the change has been merged to the master branch it is tested again.
  • If everything is OK the change is automatically deployed in all environments.
  • A tester toggles on functionality via feature-toggle in the test environment. Functionality is tested and is verified.
  • Once tested-OK a retail unit or test manager toggles on the feature.

Environments

Kitchen planner application uses three environments, dev, test, and prod. Each environment is run in a separate AWS account, creating separation.
For test and deployment pipelines two environments exists, System (prod) and SystemDev (dev). Each environment run in a separate AWS account, creating separation.
In total Kitchen planner run five environments in five different accounts.

Environment automation

Full automation, Infrastructure as Code, scripted setup of new environments.
Pipelines continuously create and discard environments.

Security tasks

  • Periodically do penetration test, performed by external company.
  • Periodically do security reviews and audits, performed by external company.
  • Run NPM audit on every pull request

Verification

Automatic tests

  • Unit tests - Performed as part of both the test and deploy pipeline.
  • Functional tests - Performed as part of both the test and deploy pipeline.
  • Integration tests - Performed as part of both the test and deploy pipeline. Also tests exposed APIs.
  • Load test - Is done periodically using load generators from IKEA Test Center

Manual tests

  • Acceptance tests - Done during BAT by business tester, usually requires features to be toggled on.
  • End to End tests - Done continuously with stakeholders from e.g. ISELL
  • Feature tests - Done during feature acceptance

Security tests

  • Security / Penetration tests - Contracted to be done by external party with each business release.

Tools

Generic

  • Git / Bitbucket - Source control.
  • Jira - Issue / task tracker.
  • Confluence - Documentation
  • AWS CodePipeline/CodeBuild/Lambda - Test and deployment pipeline

Backend code

  • Serverless framework - Infrastructure as Code, scripting deployments of infrastructure and services.
  • Node - For server side code and integration testing

Frontend code

  • React - Frontend library.
  • SASS - Styling, to be replaced by styled components.

Test and monitoring

  • Jest - Unit test framework
  • Selenium - Functional tests.
  • Protractor - Wrapper around selenium for integration with e.g. Perfecto / BrowserStack
  • Perfecto - Cloud based functional test runner.
  • Load Generator - load generators from IKEA test center.
  • Kibana - Test visualizer
  • Grafana - Log visualizer
